title: The monitorable and non-monitorable relations form Borel sets, the first comeagre and the second meagre
author: Riccardo Camerlo and Francesco Dagnino
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Theorem 3.18 of the article (source label thm:trn, source0.tex lines 726--731), the complexity theorem of the paper: both the set $\mathcal R_0$ of monitorable relations and its complement $\mathcal R_1$ are Borel subsets of $\mathcal P(X\times E\times X)$, and $\mathcal R_0$ is comeagre, equivalently $\mathcal R_1$ is meagre. It is delivered with the authors' own complete 28-line proof at source0.tex lines 733--760. H2: the proof is a genuine descriptive-set-theoretic computation rather than a qualifying examination exercise. For part (1) the solver must show first that the sets $\{R\mid q\in U_F^R\}$ are open, then translate membership in $\mathcal R_1$ into a countable sequence of conditions on finite subsets $F_0,\dots,F_N$ of $E^{<\omega}$ involving non-emptiness, pairwise disjointness and the exclusion of minimal non-empty open subsets, and conclude that those conditions are Borel. For part (2) the solver must identify a dense $\bpi^0_2$ subset, namely the relations whose associated tree is hyperconnected, verify that the defining condition is $\bpi^0_2$ in the variable $R$, and then build, inside an arbitrary basic open set of the product space, a relation containing a point that belongs to every $U_F^R$, which gives density. That combination of Borel complexity estimates with a category argument is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying level.
